seance: U04 – Rapporter des paroles : le discours indirect
resume: Rapporter ce que quelqu'un a dit (say / tell), la concordance des temps, les changements de pronoms et de repères de temps, les questions indirectes et les ordres rapportés.

sections.titre: Say et tell, concordance des temps
sections.contenu:
- ***say*** (something) : *She **said** (that) she was tired.*
- ***tell*** + **personne** : *She **told me** (that) she was tired.* (~~said me~~, ~~told that~~)

Quand le verbe introducteur est au **passé**, on **recule** les temps d'un cran :
| Paroles | Discours indirect |
| --- | --- |
| présent : *"I'm busy."* | prétérit : *He said he **was** busy.* |
| présent continu : *"I'm working."* | *He said he **was working**.* |
| prétérit / present perfect : *"I lost it." / "I've lost it."* | past perfect : *He said he **had lost** it.* |
| will : *"I'll call you."* | would : *He said he **would** call me.* |
| can : *"I can help."* | could : *He said he **could** help.* |

Si ce qui est rapporté est **toujours vrai**, le recul est facultatif : *She said she **lives** in Paris.*

sections.titre: Repères de temps et de lieu
sections.contenu:
Le point de vue change, donc les repères aussi :
| Direct | Indirect |
| --- | --- |
| *now* | *then* |
| *today / tonight* | *that day / that night* |
| *yesterday* | *the day before / the previous day* |
| *tomorrow* | *the next day / the following day* |
| *next week* | *the following week* |
| *ago* | *before* |
| *here / this* | *there / that* |

Et les **pronoms** : *"I like **your** idea," Tom told me* → *Tom told me (that) **he** liked **my** idea.*

**Questions** : on utilise ***asked***, et l'ordre redevient **sujet + verbe** (plus d'inversion, plus de *do/did*, pas de point d'interrogation) :
- *"Where do you live?"* → *She asked me where **I lived**.*
- question fermée → ***if / whether*** : *"Are you free?"* → *He asked **if I was** free.*

Même règle pour les **questions polies** : *Could you tell me where the station **is**?* (pas ~~where is the station~~) · *Do you know what time it **starts**?*

**Ordres, demandes** : ***tell / ask*** + personne + ***(not) to*** + base :
- *"Close the door."* → *He told me **to close** the door.*
- *"Don't be late."* → *She asked us **not to be** late.*

cartes.question: Complète : He ___ me he was leaving.
« I'll send it tomorrow. » → She said she ___ it the next day.
« I saw him yesterday. » → She said she had seen him ___.

cartes.recto: Rapporte : Paul: « I'm moving to Canada next month. »
cartes.verso: *Paul said (that) he **was moving** to Canada **the following month**.*

cartes.question: « Where is the meeting room? » → He asked me where ___.
Formule polie correcte :
choix: Could you tell me what time the shop opens?
Could you tell me what time does the shop open?
Could you tell me what time opens the shop?
Could you tell me what time the shop does open?
cartes.explication: Question indirecte : pas d'auxiliaire do, ordre sujet-verbe.

cartes.enonce: Rapporte cette conversation avec ton chef : « Can you work on Saturday? Don't forget the report. I'll pay you extra. »
etapes: Question fermée : He asked me if I could …
Ordre négatif : He told me not to …
will → would : He said he would …
cartes.reponse: *My boss asked me if I could work on Saturday. He told me not to forget the report and said he would pay me extra.*
